title: Applied anatomy: the gluteal region, sciatic nerve and safe intramuscular injection

header.contentArea: Surgical anatomy: gluteal region and hip

related.why: The hip joint and femoral head blood supply
Hip examination, including the Trendelenburg test
Examining for foot drop and L5 root signs

brief.scenario: Mrs Angela Treloar, 68, is on day 1 after a right total hip replacement through a posterior approach. She is nauseated and an intramuscular antiemetic has been prescribed.
brief.task: Answer the examiner's questions on the deep structures of the gluteal region, the sciatic nerve, safe intramuscular injection and the nerves at risk in hip surgery.

beforeYouWalkIn.frame: Piriformis is the key: above it the superior gluteal nerve, below it the sciatic.
beforeYouWalkIn.trap: Swapping the nerves: sciatic is at risk posteriorly, superior gluteal laterally.
beforeYouWalkIn.firstMove: "I'd use the ventrogluteal site, away from the sciatic nerve."

grid.label: Describes the deep gluteal structures
grid.fail: Cannot use piriformis as the landmark, or places the sciatic nerve above it.
grid.pass: Describes gluteus medius, piriformis, the sciatic nerve below it and the short external rotators deep to gluteus maximus.
grid.high: Places the superior gluteal nerve and vessels above piriformis and the inferior gluteal nerve and vessels below it.

grid.label: Course of the sciatic nerve
grid.fail: Cannot describe where the sciatic nerve leaves the pelvis or runs.
grid.pass: Leaves through the greater sciatic foramen below piriformis, runs deep to gluteus maximus between ischial tuberosity and greater trochanter.
grid.high: Lies on the short external rotators and quadratus femoris; its common fibular division lies laterally.

grid.label: Ventrogluteal technique
grid.fail: Gives 'upper outer buttock' with no landmarks.
grid.pass: Heel of hand on the greater trochanter, index finger on the anterior superior iliac spine, middle finger along the iliac crest; inject in the V.
grid.high: Uses the opposite hand to the hip, injects into gluteus medius, and avoids the operated side.

grid.label: Why ventrogluteal rather than dorsogluteal
grid.fail: Cannot explain why one site is safer.
grid.pass: Ventrogluteal is well away from the sciatic nerve and gluteal vessels; dorsogluteal injection can injure the sciatic nerve.
grid.high: Knows the injury is avoidable yet still reported, with potentially permanent deficit.

grid.label: Nerves at risk by approach
grid.fail: Names the superior gluteal nerve as the nerve at risk in the posterior approach.
grid.pass: Posterior approach: sciatic nerve, protected when the short rotators are reflected over it. Lateral approach: superior gluteal nerve.
grid.high: Superior gluteal nerve is at risk if gluteus medius is split more than 5 cm above the trochanter; injury gives a Trendelenburg gait.

grid.label: Postoperative foot drop
grid.pass: Examines ankle and hamstring power and sensation, distinguishing sciatic from common fibular injury; urgent senior orthopaedic review.
grid.high: Knows the fibular division is usually affected; looks for haematoma, limb lengthening and pressure at the fibular neck.

failures.move: Injecting the upper outer buttock without landmarks.
failures.consequence: The needle can reach the sciatic nerve.

failures.move: Naming the superior gluteal nerve for the posterior approach.
failures.consequence: The sciatic nerve, the structure actually at risk, is not protected.

failures.move: Attributing postoperative foot drop to anaesthesia without examining.
failures.consequence: A treatable haematoma or compression is missed.

recovery.line: Correction: sciatic posteriorly, superior gluteal laterally.
Greater trochanter, anterior superior iliac spine, iliac crest: inject in the triangle.

knowledge.fact: Above piriformis: superior gluteal nerve and vessels. Below: sciatic, inferior gluteal nerve and vessels.
Ventrogluteal: hand on the greater trochanter, index finger on the anterior superior iliac spine, inject in the V into gluteus medius.
Dorsogluteal injection can injure the sciatic nerve.
Superior gluteal nerve: safe zone up to 5 cm above the trochanter when splitting gluteus medius.
Nerve palsy after hip replacement usually affects the fibular division; posterior approach and lengthening increase risk.

recall.think: Permanent foot drop from a needle or a retractor.
recall.say: "Ventrogluteal site; sciatic at risk posteriorly, superior gluteal laterally."
do: Trochanter, ASIS, iliac crest: inject in the V

numbers.meaning: Safe split of gluteus medius above the trochanter

recall.trap: 'Upper outer quadrant' sounds safe but needs precise landmarks.
recall.finish: Ventrogluteal injection on the non-operated side; urgent review of foot drop.

reveals.trigger: Candidate asks which hip was operated on
reveals.finding: Right total hip replacement, posterior approach, yesterday.
Weak ankle and toe dorsiflexion and eversion; plantarflexion and hamstrings normal; numb dorsum of foot. Tight bandage over the fibular neck.

curveballs.prompt: So the upper outer quadrant is the same as the ventrogluteal site?
curveballs.safeAnswer: No: ventrogluteal is found from the trochanter and ASIS and is further from the sciatic nerve.

curveballs.prompt: She has a Trendelenburg gait after a lateral approach.
curveballs.safeAnswer: Superior gluteal nerve injury or abductor weakness.
